user.title: Connect to your ICT Protege
user.description:
Enter the controller's address and a WX web interface operator created just for Home Assistant. HTTPS must be enabled on the controller (firmware 4.00.1676 or later).

Home Assistant then looks for the Automation and Control service. If it answers, it is used for control (pushed live, and arm codes are checked by the panel) and the operator only reads names, so it only needs to view programming. If it doesn't, everything goes through the web interface, so give the operator's role rights to view status and the event log and to control only the areas, doors and outputs you want.

data_description.control_port: The IP Port of the Automation and Control service, if your controller has the Automation licence (usually 21000).

web.title: Web interface only
web.description:
No Automation and Control service answered on port {port}, so Home Assistant will work through the web interface. It polls the event log every couple of seconds. If your controller has the Automation licence, go back and check the service is enabled and started instead.

The web interface arms as the operator and never sees a code, so choose how codes work.

names.title: Names and zone settings from the WX web interface
names.description: The control service has no names or zone settings, so they are read from the controller's web interface. Create a WX operator that can only view programming, and enter it here. It logs in on every start and when you press Rescan, reads names, each input's areas and input types, then logs out. Names you change in Home Assistant are kept. Leave both fields empty to stop.

data_description.wx_port: HTTPS must be enabled on the controller. Usually 443.

events.title: Event logging
events.description: Optional. Add a second Automation and Control service on the panel with its own port, and a view-only user with no control rights. The integration stays logged in on that service only to receive system events. Leave both fields empty to turn event logging off.

codes.title: Arming codes
codes.description: In web-only mode the panel never sees a code, so Home Assistant checks it. People with codes: {people}.

data_description.add_code: At least 4 digits. Stored only as a salted hash.

upgrade.title: Switch to the Automation and Control service
upgrade.description: If the controller now has the Automation licence and the service is set up, switch over: control becomes pushed live and arming codes are checked by the panel instead of Home Assistant. Your devices, entities and their history are kept, and the web operator carries on reading names and zone settings once at start-up. The integration stays on the control service from then on.

web_rights.title: Web operator can't read everything on {title}
web_rights.description: The operator's role doesn't allow reading: {boxes}. Those entities stay unavailable. To use them, tick those boxes under Monitoring on the operator's role in the WX web interface; this alert clears by itself once they can be read. If you don't need them, disable those entities instead. Outputs is optional: it lets the operator switch every output, including sirens.
